column1: # 音讀-format spellings added by the editors, for words that start in Hangul and
# so cannot be 訓讀 entries. 두벌式: the 釋讀會 chat; 세벌式: formed the same way.
# 여러 가지: typed as one word, written as two; the chat writes 여러 가지 once and keeps 가지 in Hangul
# after a Hanja numeral (三 가지, 一二가지, 幾가지).
# The common word, where FusionIME's frequencies favour a place name or a rarer homophone.
# The chat writes this word this way as a clear habit, and FusionIME's frequencies favour another homophone.
# 身上 for personal details; 身相 is the Diamond Sutra's word, the only place the chat has it.
# 器物損壞, kli.korean.go.kr/term/trgtWord/indexTrgtWord.do?trgtWordNo=223105828. The chat's 其物 reads 그것.
# 進士, encykorea.aks.ac.kr/Article/E0054718. The chat's 進賜 is the 吏讀 spelling of 나리.
# The chat writes this word in Hanja, and a split into a 訓讀 stem and an ending (酸기 for 시기) wins without this row.
# Words ending in 人 or 道, where the Hangul ending wins without this row.
# The common word, where FusionIME's frequencies favour a place name, a person or a rarer homophone, and the chat shows no habit of its own.
# The common word, where a split into a 訓讀 stem and an ending wins and the chat shows no habit of its own.
# Written whole, so 신기 inside it does not split as 神奇.
# 胡桃: 山林廳's walnut reference gives 호도(胡桃), forest.go.kr/kfs/images/data/down/imsan/imsan_01_05.pdf;
# 胡桃菓子 in a historical document, minjok.or.kr/archives/144553. 국립국어원 records 호두과자(-菓子), the second candidate.
# 地圖 (the chat 16×, 指導 once). The engine keeps 지도 after ㄹ for the ending -ㄹ지도.
# Sino-Korean words the chat writes in Hanja, ahead of a commoner homophone (2026-11-06).
# 후 "after": the chat writes 後 (百年後, 後에). 후타나리 and 후리가나 are loanwords that start with it.
# 구시대: ahead of a verb reading of its first syllables.
# 재일한인: two listed words, ahead of the prefix 再.
# 무지방: 脂肪, ahead of the commoner 地方 after the prefix 無.
